M O R E   M A I L ! !

  November, 1993      Page Reply

 How to write to us...02     -

 John Cleveland.......03    23

 Andy Davis...........25     -

 Barry Edgeway........27     -

 Francis Miles........29    34

 C. Leslie Pollard....37    41

 Chris Ingram.........43    44

   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From John Cleveland, LONDON

Dear Ron & Brian,

I can still remember wondering
what use I could find for Dom-
inic Morris's +3 TAPER utility
when it appeared in OUTLET no.
69.Well,now I've found a perfect
use, namely direct transfer of
files from +3 disc to the PC
running the Lunter Spectrum emu-
lator(reviewed by Paul Oliver in
Outlet no. 73).

This requires a tape interface
(I use the one supplied by B.G.
Services) plugged into the PC's
parallel printer port and linked
directly by the usual +3 tape
lead to the tape output on the
+3.

One types LOAD "" or LOAD""CODE
on the PC and runs TAPER on the
+3. I've transferred dozens and
dozens of files this way with
relatively few "tape loading
errors". The beauty of this
method is its directness and the
fact that you don't have to
carry out tiresome conversion
processes as you do on files
transferred by other methods,
e.g.,via RS232 or 3.5" disc.

When SAVEing transferred pro-
grams on the PC, it may be
necessary to know the autorun
line number for BASIC, and the
address and length for CODE.
This information can be obtained
from the +3 disc with the aid of
EXTENDACAT (OUTLET no. 37).


Alternatively one can SAVE auto-
matically with UNITRANS+ (from
OUTLET EXTRA 1) on the PC. If
this is run in"Manual" mode then
every time the SAVE prompt comes
up one has the opportunity not
only of changing the microdrive
syntax to tape syntax(for saving
to a .TAP file) but also of
amending the filename, e.g. to
remove any superfluous full-stop
divider TAPER has added to the
filename or to add the mysteri-
ous spaces which occur in some
OUTLET filenames,eg,"EDIT'L .#",
as defined in line 30 of the
CONTENTS program.

It's almost as easy to transfer
a program in the emulator memory
to the +3, but this time a
cassette recorder must be used.

The MIC socket of the recorder
is connected to the output of
the tape interface, and its EAR
socket to the +3 tape input.


Set the recorder to record, do
LOAD on the +3 and SAVE on the
PC, and forget about what is
recorded on the tape because
this is a one-step operation in
which the recorder acts merely
as a sort of in-line amplifier.


Of course, all this transferring
to and fro assumes that the
appropriate input and output
settings have been made in the
emulator's tape interface menu
(called up with F7).


A happy bonus of the above
arrangements (taken together) is
that tape software can be loaded
into the +3 or the PC or both
simultaneously (!!) without any
plugging or unplugging of leads.
You can even load on the PC
while monitoring with CAT "t:"
on the +3. This is because the
+3, provided it's switched on,
merrily passes on any input it
receives on the tape input lead
to the tape output lead.

For transferring WORDMASTER/
HEADLINER/TYPELINER files,
however, it is advisable to use
WORDMASTER's own load/save
facilities. I've got the tape
version of WORDMASTER running in
48K + I'F1 mode on the PC, while
the +3 runs its own version.

One simply loads a file off the
+3 disc and then SAVEs it to
drive "T" while simultaneously
LOADing from drive "0" at the PC
end. Transfer also works in the
other direction (with the aid of
the cassette recorder) -in fact,
I wrote this letter in
WORDMASTER on the PC then sent
it across to the +3 for final
correction while spell-checking
an ASCII copy in LocoScript PC.

You can print from WORDMASTER on
the PC provided the command OPEN
#3;"b" has been issued in BASIC.
As on the +3,I prefer the alter-
native screen character set
"minicharsW" from OUTLET no. 23,
and reduce the jumpiness of the
cursor keys with: POKE 64193,13:
POKE 64194,24.

It is also possible to alter the
text of some of the menu options
to make them more PC-friendly,
e.g. by changing [INV.VID] to
[CAPS-4]. This is most easily
done on the +3 by locating and
amending the menu text with the
aid of the Multiface 3 toolkit,
then returning the amended code
file to the PC.


There are design problems in the
way the Emulator handles
simulated tape (.TAP) files on
disc. Paul Oliver, in his
review, has already touched on
the problem with successive
SAVEs of the same filename in
"multiple .TAP file mode".


What bugs me more though is the
way files are LOADed from disc
in "single .TAP file mode" where
the Emulator puts up large blue
information boxes displaying the
header information of all the
blocks in turn as it lurches
through them searching for the
one it wants.

These boxes, while entirely
appropriate when loading from
REAL tape, seem unnecessary and
inappropriate when dealing with
disc files, and enormously slow
down the search for the desired
block. Isn't it pain enough
having the Speccy ROM write
filenames to the screen, without
the Emulator pitching in its own
four pennyworth?


Something else that needs remedy
is the absence of a CAT or DIR
facility to catalogue DOS
directories. This is a function
which should be assigned to one
of the function keys, e.g. F5,
in place of the improbable "NMI"
facility (which is already prov-
ided for in the"Extra Functions"
menu). Something that would be
particularly useful would be a
CATLOADER-like facility for cat-
aloguing and loading .Z80 files.

Some improvements could also be
made in the keyboard mapping of
certain characters. Take the
double quotes sign for example -
this cannot be obtained with the
usual UK PC keyboard stroke
(caps-shifted 2). Instead you


have either to use ALT-P(corres-
ponding to the Spectrum SYMB-P)
or caps-shifted single-quote,
which suggests to me the author
has been using a US keyboard (I
would not have thought the Spec-
trum's transatlantic market
penetration was sufficient to
warrant such a choice).

Another example is the close
bracket ")" which is obtained by
ALT "(", i.e. using the OPEN
bracket key.

This is all very confusing - in
fact you really need to develop
a sort of split personality to
be able to keep switching
between the normal PC keystrokes
and the invisible Spectrum key-
board map.

Maybe that explains why every
time I walk down the street I
seem to see men in white coats
peering at me from behind the
bushes!

On the broader scale, I'd like
to see better Emulator support
for the +3, preferably a full-
blown +3 emulation and a utility
for converting Multiface 3 snap-
shots to .Z80 files. This latter
is necessary not least because
some of the overprotected games
software of recent years won't
readily load into the emulator,
even though it loads O.K. on a
real Spectrum (Mirrorsoft's
TETRIS is an example - I tried
loading it in different modes
and with various settings but to
no avail.).

I know of two ways round this
problem. The first is to make a
+D snapshot which is then conv-
erted to .Z80 with the utility
provided for this purpose in the
registered version of the Emul-
ator.The second method,for those
(including myself) without a +D,
is to make a Multiface 3 snap-
shot then use Tony Summerfield's
"M3UNLOCK" (which I reviewed in
Issue 14 of"+3 Contact"(R.I.P.))
to convert the M3 files into a
series of ordinary CODE files
with a BASIC loader. These are
then transferred to the PC, run,
and snapped to .Z80.Both methods
work with TETRIS. I've used
M3UNLOCK many times and can only
recall one failure (I think that
was SCRABBLE).


It would also be worthwhile if
the Emulator could get the PC
mouse to emulate the Kempston
mouse, for the benefit of Art
Studio, Artist 2, Music Writer,
etc. Oh, and wouldn't it be nice
if a fix could be found for that
pestilential Spectrum bug which
makes the cursor keys periodic-
ally print numbers instead of
moving the cursor.

Notwithstanding my gripes, the
Lunter emulator is certainly a
magnificent achievement and a
major landmark in Spectrum hist-
ory - indeed it guarantees the
survival of the Spectrum long
after its original hardware has
passed on to the great computer
empyrean aloft.


The benefits of hard disc
support and of the superior PC
keyboard and monitors cannot be
understated. (Mind you, on my
monitor Spectrum CIRCLEs come
out looking like Easter eggs!)

The chunky font of OUTLET text
files comes out especially well
on my monitor, and you can even
page back and forth with the PC
joystick (something that doesn't
work on a real Spectrum - in
fact I seem to remember you once
turning down a reader's request
for joystick control.)

Similarly ye olde Spectrum cur-
sor-key-controlled games, such
as the original Psion Flight
Simulator,are also now joystick-


controllable, as is the text
cursor in WORDMASTER (- handy
for scrolling up and down). That
is interesting because the joy-
stick has no effect in "proper"
DOS wordprocessors such as Loco-
Script and WordPerfect. Another
case of one-up for the Speccy
and its software, n'est-ce-pas?


Most PCs, including my own, have
only one parallel printer port,
and it's a right old pain having
to keep unplugging the printer
to fit the tape interface and
vice versa. As far as I know
there is no single piece of kit
on the market which can solve
this problem.


As a temporary expedient, I've
redeployed the 2-way Centronics
data switch box which has
hitherto served to switch the
printer between the PC and the
+3, so that it now switches the
PC printer port between the tape
interface and the printer. The
tape interface is connected via
a gender changer (Maplin JM49D)
to the 25-pin plug of a standard
PC printer cable, the other end
of which is plugged into the
switch box.

This works splendidly, but it's
a gratuitously expensive set-up
unless you already have all the
components and cables. (The
Maplin equivalent of my switch
box is probably ZA64U.)


I've been experimenting with
converting a +3 issue of OUTLET
to run in the emulator. The best
- or rather, least awful -
method I've come up with so far
is to transfer the files with
the TAPER-UNITRANS technique
described above, and SAVE them
in a single .TAP file, starting
with DISK and CONTENTS, then the
remaining programs in their
CONTENTS order.


"Multiple .TAP file mode" is
inappropriate if more than one
issue of OUTLET is stored owing
to some programs (e.g. CONTENTS
itself) having the same filename
in all OUTLETs.


The trouble with single .TAP
mode though is those flashing
blue boxes I mentioned earlier,
which retard and disfigure the
movement from one program to
another. Perhaps you know a
better way of going about it, or
will the Disciple emulator fore-
shadowed in Brian Gaff's letter
last month solve the problem?


By the way,is there any prospect
of a PC Spectrum Emulator vers-
ion of OUTLET (as distinct from
the already projected PC DOS
version)? May we look forward to
some happy day when all OUTLETs,
right back to the first issue,
are available in Emulator-
friendly form?


It's not my usual custom to blow
good money on overpriced child-
ren's comics, but, driven by a
spirit of misguided nostalgia, I
decided to make an exception for
the last-ever edition (issue 93)
of Your Sinclair. But could I
find a newsagent in London with
one to sell? Could I heck! And
by the time I got round to
writing off to YS Back Issues,
the cupboard was bare. (Sigh!)

Last month's OUTLET (no. 74)
certainly was a scintillating
bumper bundle, and the inclusion
of AlchNews and the PD lists
added most interestingly to the
diversity. Will you include
future issues and PD lists &
updates in OUTLET? - I hope so.


Lastly,a query about TAPERMOD in
OUTLET no. 73. (side A of the +3
disc).This contains an instruct-
ion to "delete this line" after
merging with "TAPER",despite it-
self consisting only of a single
program line. Hmmm.

             Yours,

        John Cleveland

Brian Cavers to John Cleveland

There's a great new +3 extended
CAT utility in next month's OUT-
LET named CATDB.It's much faster
than EXTENDACAT and works on any
format.

Our microdrive CATLOADER works
fine on the emulator with the
pseudo-microdrives and we are
currently looking at how to make
it available for those who don't
have real microdrives.

Regarding your printer,you could
get a three-way printer switch.

TAPERMOD should have read "enter
'GO TO 9952' or 'RUN 9952' then
delete line 9952 and resave the
program."!!!!

I've thought about converting
microdrive back issues to the PC
emulator and even re-introducing
a PC microdrive version but I'm
so desparately short of time I
absolutely MUST concentrate on
getting the main PC version on
the road.

We shall probably include other
ALCHNEWS and PD lists within
OUTLET from time to time.

Regarding the men in white coats
- just because you are paranoid
doesn't necessarily mean that
they are not really out to get
you.
                       - Brian

           Andy Davis

From Barry Edgeway, Norfolk.



Dear Ron and Brian,

I am having a wonderful time
going through the back issues of
Outlet as I had no chance during
the spring and summer (through
work commitments) of reading
Outlet on a monthly basis.

I last wrote to you in November
'92 with some printing problems
and snapshot file problems. Both
those problems are now solved,
with thanks to you and contrib-
utors of Outlet. I just wish I
could make contributions like
some of the members do.


I have noticed an error in the
CALCULAR program in Issue May,
93. It calculates 3.78 Litres
per gallon which is in fact U.S.
gallons not imperial gallons as
in England which is 4.545 Litres
per gallon.If it was not spotted
before I hope it's of some use
to someone who suddenly realised
there was something drastically
wrong with their car using too
much petrol.

Outlet is such a useful magazine
I hope you get the support you
deserve.

            Yours sincerely,

             Barry Edgeway

From Francis Miles, WELWYN


Dear Ron and Brian,

I've been rereading the corres-
pondence about centrifugal force
- I put in my fourpenceworth in
OUTLET 64 and thought I'd noth-
ing more to say, but perhaps I
have!

The problem is one of termino-
logy, that is to say everybody
understands well enough what's
going on but because it's not
quite like other similar situ-
ations the words used to desc-
ribe it don't quite fit. Quite a
common problem in applied sci-
ence - consider electronics!


Four situations:

1. You and a friend pull on the
ends of a piece of string.

2. He ties his end to a post and
leaves you pulling on the other.

3. You tie your end to another
post and leave the string
stretched tight between them.

4. You tie a stone to the end of
another string and whirl it
round your head.

Ask yourself: what forces are
acting in each of these situa-
tions? Which is Newton's "act-
ion" and which is "reaction"?

My answers...

1.You and your friend are each
 exerting a force.The string is
 slightly elastic so is stretch-
 ed and is pulling back against
 each of you. Four forces in
 equilibrium.
2.The post is also slightly ela-
 stic so it bends a little. This
 exerts a force on the string
 replacing your friend's pull.
 Otherwise just like 1.
3.Just like 2 but with the 2nd
  post now supplying the pull
  you were exerting.
4.Different from all of 1.-3.,
  because the forces aren't in
 equilibrium - as is clear from
 the fact that the system is in
 constant motion, not in a
 straight line. There are only
 three obvious forces...


  4.1 your pull on the string
  4.2 and 4.3 the tension in the
      string pulling both ways.

The "centripetal" force in the
string (4.3) pulls the stone off
its course so that it doesn't
fly off at a tangent. The only
"centrifugal" force here is 4.2,
the tension in the string pull-
ing on your hand.Centripetal and
centrifugal are not words with
any arcane meaning: they just
mean "going towards the centre"
and "going away from the centre"

Actually there is a fourth force
the stone is slightly compressed
where the string holds it, and
pushes back against the string.
This is another "centrifugal"
force.

If you want to be confused fur-
ther, try the Einsteinian situ-
ations 5. and 6.:

5. You hang the stone on the end
of its string down a well.

6. You hoist it up from the well
with constant acceleration.

        Yours sincerely,

        FRANCIS G MILES.

Brian Cavers to Francis Miles


Consider the following...

You're hung up by your toes by
some stout cord with your head
in a bucket of custard which is
also suspended by a cord.

If you spin round you will coil,
and therefore shorten, the cord
which is tied to your toes and
gradually pull your head out of
the custard.

However, at the same time I am
rotating the bucket which is
therefore also coiling the cord
which supports it and is also
gradually rising.


There are several forces to
consider.Let's consider them for
a while. Ten minutes OK?

You could swallow some of the
custard.

I could mix some more. Do you
like the sugar-free? It's better
for your health.

If I let go of the bucket it
will rotate rapidly and descend
but then its momentum will make
it wind up the cord again. This
will repeat so you will get a
breather now and again.

The number of breaths you get in
any given period depends on many
different factors...

 1. The depth of the bucket
 2. The mass of the bucket
 3. The depth of the custard
 4. The thickness of the custard
 5. The flavour of the custard
 6. The size of your head
 7. The mass of your head
 8. The length of the cords
 9. The thickness of the cords
10. The size of your toes
11. The number of twizzles.

6 and 10 might vary with time. I
could plot a size/time graph.

I do find the contemplation of
experimental physics so very
satisfying. What do you think?
Pardon? Sorry - I can't hear you
clearly. More custard anyone?
                         - Brian

From C. Leslie Pollard, HERTS


Dear Brian,

 Re: MUSICFILE V.2 in OUTLET 74

Sorry to be such a nuisance but
I still cannot get MUSIFILE to
work!!!

Although empty, the first  entry
is 856.9375 and it doesn't tran-
sfer any entry into memory and
soon crashes on any attempt to
investigate.

I have a Disciple and 48K+ and I
thought that it was interchange-
able with all +D programs; per-
haps it is not so in this case.


I am all agog to use this pro-
gram which, even for OUTLET
programs, exceeds one's expect-
ations!

On the first version I did all
the changes and SAVEd my long
list of composer data; this was
before I knew it would not work.
I also had to remove acres of
unused other interfaces etc and
other unused lines as Chris
said. This to gve me memory of
which I ran out. I assume that
this is OK to just leave the
Disciple reference for printout.


I assume that when I can get it
working I shall be able to merge
my list. What I can tell you is:


1. New entries start 856.9375;
subesequently,857.9375,858.9375.

2. Although it says it is trans-
ferring to memory, it does not.

3. On trying to retrieve inputs,
it call the first entry No.856
then says "no such entry". If I
am not alone you must be bless-
ing this magic program!

4.I only found a few alterations
in the listing so I thought I'd
better check before wasting any
more time.

I suppose that when working
correctly it starts from entry
No.1. The entry number seems
necessary for more than one
title etc. on C, T or V.

On the demo printout I managed,
it correctly showed the C, T or
V number but not the entry
number.

Again, sorry for the trouble.

          Best wishes,

       C. Leslie Pollard

Brian Cavers to C.Leslie Pollard

I'm sorry you have had all this
trouble and wasted effort. We
only gave it a cursory test with
the demo data and it seemed OK.
Now I have tried it with new
data I got the same as you - it
just does not put the input in
memory.

I have scanned the BASIC and it
does appear to do some POKEs but
it it might take me ages to see
if I can do anything with it and
it would be wiser to wait for
the author (who hopefully will
read this) to comment.

Meanwhile, I urge you to try the
brilliant MASTERFILE in this
issue...

The 48K MASTERFILE is simple to
use if you follow the instruct-
ions and PRACTICE THE EXAMPLES.
Once you have the hang of it,you
will find it much more flexible
and powerful.

            - Brian

From Chris Ingram, MALAWI

Has anyone else had reported
difficulties using MUSIC FILE
with anything other than the
demo?

I tried entering my own data
including a new composer list-
and got only gibberish, the
entry numbers showing impossible
decimal for example.

         Chris Ingram

Brian Cavers to Chris Ingram

Sorry - there are problems with
MUSIC FILE. I think you may be
referring to the original one
but the new version in Issue 74
is bugged too (see the OUTLETTER
from C. Leslie Pollard in this
issue).

Hang on until we hear from the
author, Jim Hossack. Meanwhile,
I recommend you try MASTERFILE
in this issue.

             Brian.

You can print from WORDMASTER on the PC provided the command OPEN #3;"b" has been issued in BASIC. As on the +3,I prefer the alter- native screen character set "minicharsW" from OUTLET no. 23, and reduce the jumpiness of the cursor keys with: POKE 64193,13: POKE 64194,24.

It is also possible to alter the text of some of the menu options to make them more PC-friendly, e.g. by changing [INV.VID] to [CAPS-4]. This is most easily done on the +3 by locating and amending the menu text with the aid of the Multiface 3 toolkit, then returning the amended code file to the PC.

There are design problems in the way the Emulator handles simulated tape (.TAP) files on disc. Paul Oliver, in his review, has already touched on the problem with successive SAVEs of the same filename in "multiple .TAP file mode".

What bugs me more though is the way files are LOADed from disc in "single .TAP file mode" where the Emulator puts up large blue information boxes displaying the header information of all the blocks in turn as it lurches through them searching for the one it wants.

These boxes, while entirely appropriate when loading from REAL tape, seem unnecessary and inappropriate when dealing with disc files, and enormously slow down the search for the desired block. Isn't it pain enough having the Speccy ROM write filenames to the screen, without the Emulator pitching in its own four pennyworth?

Something else that needs remedy is the absence of a CAT or DIR facility to catalogue DOS directories. This is a function which should be assigned to one of the function keys, e.g. F5, in place of the improbable "NMI" facility (which is already prov- ided for in the"Extra Functions" menu). Something that would be particularly useful would be a CATLOADER-like facility for cat- aloguing and loading .Z80 files.

Some improvements could also be made in the keyboard mapping of certain characters. Take the double quotes sign for example - this cannot be obtained with the usual UK PC keyboard stroke (caps-shifted 2). Instead you

have either to use ALT-P(corres- ponding to the Spectrum SYMB-P) or caps-shifted single-quote, which suggests to me the author has been using a US keyboard (I would not have thought the Spec- trum's transatlantic market penetration was sufficient to warrant such a choice).

Another example is the close bracket ")" which is obtained by ALT "(", i.e. using the OPEN bracket key.

This is all very confusing - in fact you really need to develop a sort of split personality to be able to keep switching between the normal PC keystrokes and the invisible Spectrum key- board map.

Maybe that explains why every time I walk down the street I seem to see men in white coats peering at me from behind the bushes!

On the broader scale, I'd like to see better Emulator support for the +3, preferably a full- blown +3 emulation and a utility for converting Multiface 3 snap- shots to .Z80 files. This latter is necessary not least because some of the overprotected games software of recent years won't readily load into the emulator, even though it loads O.K. on a real Spectrum (Mirrorsoft's TETRIS is an example - I tried loading it in different modes and with various settings but to no avail.).

I know of two ways round this problem. The first is to make a +D snapshot which is then conv- erted to .Z80 with the utility provided for this purpose in the registered version of the Emul- ator.The second method,for those (including myself) without a +D, is to make a Multiface 3 snap- shot then use Tony Summerfield's "M3UNLOCK" (which I reviewed in Issue 14 of"+3 Contact"(R.I.P.)) to convert the M3 files into a series of ordinary CODE files with a BASIC loader. These are then transferred to the PC, run, and snapped to .Z80.Both methods work with TETRIS. I've used M3UNLOCK many times and can only recall one failure (I think that was SCRABBLE).

It would also be worthwhile if the Emulator could get the PC mouse to emulate the Kempston mouse, for the benefit of Art Studio, Artist 2, Music Writer, etc. Oh, and wouldn't it be nice if a fix could be found for that pestilential Spectrum bug which makes the cursor keys periodic- ally print numbers instead of moving the cursor.

Notwithstanding my gripes, the Lunter emulator is certainly a magnificent achievement and a major landmark in Spectrum hist- ory - indeed it guarantees the survival of the Spectrum long after its original hardware has passed on to the great computer empyrean aloft.

The benefits of hard disc support and of the superior PC keyboard and monitors cannot be understated. (Mind you, on my monitor Spectrum CIRCLEs come out looking like Easter eggs!)

The chunky font of OUTLET text files comes out especially well on my monitor, and you can even page back and forth with the PC joystick (something that doesn't work on a real Spectrum - in fact I seem to remember you once turning down a reader's request for joystick control.)

Similarly ye olde Spectrum cur- sor-key-controlled games, such as the original Psion Flight Simulator,are also now joystick-

controllable, as is the text cursor in WORDMASTER (- handy for scrolling up and down). That is interesting because the joy- stick has no effect in "proper" DOS wordprocessors such as Loco- Script and WordPerfect. Another case of one-up for the Speccy and its software, n'est-ce-pas?

Most PCs, including my own, have only one parallel printer port, and it's a right old pain having to keep unplugging the printer to fit the tape interface and vice versa. As far as I know there is no single piece of kit on the market which can solve this problem.

As a temporary expedient, I've redeployed the 2-way Centronics data switch box which has hitherto served to switch the printer between the PC and the +3, so that it now switches the PC printer port between the tape interface and the printer. The tape interface is connected via a gender changer (Maplin JM49D) to the 25-pin plug of a standard PC printer cable, the other end of which is plugged into the switch box.

This works splendidly, but it's a gratuitously expensive set-up unless you already have all the components and cables. (The Maplin equivalent of my switch box is probably ZA64U.)

I've been experimenting with converting a +3 issue of OUTLET to run in the emulator. The best - or rather, least awful - method I've come up with so far is to transfer the files with the TAPER-UNITRANS technique described above, and SAVE them in a single .TAP file, starting with DISK and CONTENTS, then the remaining programs in their CONTENTS order.

"Multiple .TAP file mode" is inappropriate if more than one issue of OUTLET is stored owing to some programs (e.g. CONTENTS itself) having the same filename in all OUTLETs.

The trouble with single .TAP mode though is those flashing blue boxes I mentioned earlier, which retard and disfigure the movement from one program to another. Perhaps you know a better way of going about it, or will the Disciple emulator fore- shadowed in Brian Gaff's letter last month solve the problem?

By the way,is there any prospect of a PC Spectrum Emulator vers- ion of OUTLET (as distinct from the already projected PC DOS version)? May we look forward to some happy day when all OUTLETs, right back to the first issue, are available in Emulator- friendly form?

It's not my usual custom to blow good money on overpriced child- ren's comics, but, driven by a spirit of misguided nostalgia, I decided to make an exception for the last-ever edition (issue 93) of Your Sinclair. But could I find a newsagent in London with one to sell? Could I heck! And by the time I got round to writing off to YS Back Issues, the cupboard was bare. (Sigh!)

I've been rereading the corres- pondence about centrifugal force - I put in my fourpenceworth in OUTLET 64 and thought I'd noth- ing more to say, but perhaps I have!

The problem is one of termino- logy, that is to say everybody understands well enough what's going on but because it's not quite like other similar situ- ations the words used to desc- ribe it don't quite fit. Quite a common problem in applied sci- ence - consider electronics!

Four situations:

1. You and a friend pull on the ends of a piece of string.

2. He ties his end to a post and leaves you pulling on the other.

3. You tie your end to another post and leave the string stretched tight between them.

4. You tie a stone to the end of another string and whirl it round your head.

Ask yourself: what forces are acting in each of these situa- tions? Which is Newton's "act- ion" and which is "reaction"?

My answers...

1.You and your friend are each exerting a force.The string is slightly elastic so is stretch- ed and is pulling back against each of you. Four forces in equilibrium. 2.The post is also slightly ela- stic so it bends a little. This exerts a force on the string replacing your friend's pull. Otherwise just like 1. 3.Just like 2 but with the 2nd post now supplying the pull you were exerting. 4.Different from all of 1.-3., because the forces aren't in equilibrium - as is clear from the fact that the system is in constant motion, not in a straight line. There are only three obvious forces...

4.1 your pull on the string 4.2 and 4.3 the tension in the string pulling both ways.

The "centripetal" force in the string (4.3) pulls the stone off its course so that it doesn't fly off at a tangent. The only "centrifugal" force here is 4.2, the tension in the string pull- ing on your hand.Centripetal and centrifugal are not words with any arcane meaning: they just mean "going towards the centre" and "going away from the centre"

Actually there is a fourth force the stone is slightly compressed where the string holds it, and pushes back against the string. This is another "centrifugal" force.

If you want to be confused fur- ther, try the Einsteinian situ- ations 5. and 6.:

5. You hang the stone on the end of its string down a well.

6. You hoist it up from the well with constant acceleration.

### От John Cleveland, LONDON

Дорогие Ron и Brian,

Я до сих пор помню, как размышлял, какое применение смогу найти утилите +3 TAPER от Dominic Morris, когда она появилась в OUTLET № 69. Что ж, теперь я нашел идеальное применение, а именно — прямой перенос файлов с дискеты +3 на PC, на котором запущен Spectrum-эмулятор Lunter (на него Paul Oliver делал обзор в Outlet № 73).

Для этого требуется tape interface (я использую адаптер от B.G. Services), подключенный к параллельному порту принтера на PC и соединенный напрямую обычным шнуром для магнитофона +3 с выходом tape на +3.

На PC набирается `LOAD ""` или `LOAD "" CODE`, а на +3 запускается TAPER. Таким способом я перенес десятки и десятки файлов с относительно небольшим числом «tape loading errors». Прелесть этого метода заключается в его прямоте и в том, что вам не нужно выполнять утомительные процедуры конверсии, как это бывает при переносе другими способами, например, через RS232 или 3.5" дискету.

При сохранении (SAVE) перенесенных программ на PC может потребоваться знание номера строки автозапуска для BASIC, а также адреса и длины для CODE. Эту информацию можно получить с диска +3 с помощью EXTENDACAT (OUTLET № 37).

Кроме того, можно сохранять автоматически с помощью UNITRANS+ (из OUTLET EXTRA 1) на PC. Если запустить ее в режиме «Manual», то каждый раз при появлении приглашения SAVE у вас будет возможность не только изменить синтаксис microdrive на синтаксис tape (для сохранения в файл .TAP), но и подкорректировать имя файла — например, убрать лишнюю точку-разделитель, которую TAPER добавил к имени, или добавить таинственные пробелы, встречающиеся в некоторых именах файлов OUTLET, например, "EDIT'L .#", как задано в строке 30 программы CONTENTS.

Перенести программу из памяти эмулятора обратно на +3 почти так же просто, но на этот раз придется использовать кассетный магнитофон.

Гнездо MIC магнитофона подключается к выходу tape interface, а его гнездо EAR — ко входу tape на +3.

Включите магнитофон на запись, выполните LOAD на +3 и SAVE на PC, и забудьте о том, что записывается на ленту, поскольку это одношаговая операция, в которой магнитофон выступает лишь в роли своего рода промежуточного усилителя.

Разумеется, все эти переброски туда и обратно предполагают, что в меню tape interface эмулятора (вызываемом по F7) выставлены соответствующие настройки входа и выхода.

Приятный бонус от всех этих манипуляций (взятых вместе) заключается в том, что ленточный софт можно загружать на +3, на PC или на оба компьютера одновременно (!!) без перетыкания проводов. Вы даже можете загружать программу на PC, отслеживая процесс с помощью `CAT "t:"` на +3. Это связано с тем, что +3, если он включен, весело транслирует любой сигнал, поступающий на его входной магнитофонный разъем, прямо на выходной.

Однако для переноса файлов WORDMASTER / HEADLINER / TYPELINER рекомендуется использовать собственные функции загрузки/сохранения WORDMASTER. У меня на PC ленточная версия WORDMASTER работает в режиме 48K + I'F1, в то время как на +3 запущена своя версия.

Вы просто загружаете файл с диска +3, затем сохраняете (SAVE) его на диск «T», одновременно выполняя загрузку (LOAD) с диска «0» на стороне PC. Перенос работает и в обратном направлении (с помощью кассетного магнитофона) — фактически, я написал это письмо в WORDMASTER на PC, а затем переслал его на +3 для окончательной правки, попутно проверяя орфографию ASCII-копии в LocoScript PC.

Печатать из WORDMASTER на PC можно при условии, что в BASIC была отдана команда `OPEN #3;"b"`. Как и на +3, я предпочитаю альтернативный экранный набор символов «minicharsW» из OUTLET № 23, а излишнюю прыгучесть клавиш курсора уменьшаю с помощью: `POKE 64193,13: POKE 64194,24`.

Также можно изменить текст некоторых пунктов меню, чтобы сделать их более дружественными к PC, например, заменив [INV.VID] на [CAPS-4]. Проще всего это сделать на +3, найдя и исправив текст меню с помощью инструментария Multiface 3, а затем вернув измененный кодовый файл обратно на PC.

В том, как эмулятор работает с виртуальными ленточными файлами (.TAP) на диске, есть конструктивные недочеты. Paul Oliver в своем обзоре уже коснулся проблемы последовательных SAVE с одинаковым именем файла в режиме «multiple .TAP file mode».

Но еще больше меня раздражает то, как файлы загружаются (LOAD) с диска в режиме «single .TAP file mode», когда эмулятор выводит большие синие информационные окна, отображающие данные заголовка всех блоков подряд по мере того, как он неуклюже перебирает их в поисках нужного.

Эти окна, будучи совершенно уместными при загрузке с РЕАЛЬНОЙ кассеты, кажутся ненужными и неуместными при работе с дисковыми файлами и чудовищно замедляют поиск нужного блока. Неужели мало того, что Speccy ROM выводит имена файлов на экран — нужно ли эмулятору обязательно вставлять свои пять копеек?

Еще одна вещь, требующая исправления, — это отсутствие функции CAT или DIR для просмотра каталогов DOS. Эту функцию стоило бы назначить на одну из функциональных клавиш, например F5, вместо маловероятной функции «NMI» (которая и так предусмотрена в меню «Extra Functions»). Особенно полезной была бы функция в стиле CATLOADER для каталогизации и загрузки файлов .Z80.

Кое-какие улучшения можно было бы внести и в раскладку клавиатуры для определенных символов. Возьмем, к примеру, знак двойных кавычек — его нельзя ввести привычной комбинацией британской клавиатуры PC (Caps Shift + 2). Вместо этого приходится либо использовать Alt-P (соответствующий спектрумовскому Symb-P), либо одинарную кавычку с Caps Shift, что наводит меня на мысль об использовании автором американской клавиатуры (не думаю, что проникновение Spectrum на заокеанский рынок было достаточным, чтобы оправдать такой выбор).
